College Football Ratings

Ratings are built from drives. At the start of each possession, the offense has some number of yards to the goal line available; the rating is the share of those available yards the offense gained, adjusted for the quality of the opponents faced. Off: the share of available yards an offense gains (higher is better). Def: the share a defense allows (lower is better). Net = Off minus Def, in percentage points. SOS is the average opposing offense faced minus the average opposing defense faced, so positive means a tougher schedule. Garbage time is excluded, and only games between FBS teams count toward the ratings. Small numbers next to a value are its national rank. Records and point differential are as of the selected week. Through a team's first 8 games, its rating is a blend of its final rating from last season and its rating from this season so far: with g games played, this season counts for g/8 and last season for the rest. The This Yr column shows that share. The Preseason view is last season's final ratings.
